source.method: Each player's WAR (JEFFBAGWELL: the average of Baseball-Reference's and FanGraphs' WAR) per playing time over the season and the two before it, weighted 5, 3 and 2 (relievers 1, 1 and 1) and regressed toward a level below replacement: hitters 600 × (Σ weight·WAR − 9) / (Σ weight·PA + 600); starters 180 × (Σ weight·WAR − 4.5) / (Σ weight·IP + 150); relievers 65 × (Σ WAR − 1.5) / (Σ IP + 30) + 0.8 × the season's average leverage index. Roles and positions from his games, starts and innings, his club his last. docs/design/baseball.md, "Seasons before 2018: computed from WAR".
source.conversion: Rank for rank within each role (hitters, starters, relievers) onto MLB The Show 18 to 24's overalls at the same depth per club: the k-th best score of a season of T clubs takes the overall at index (k − 0.5) / T × 210 − 0.5 of that role's 9,674-card reference, strongest first (scripts/data/mlb-war-reference.json), interpolated and rounded; equal scores share their mean rank. Then each club moves toward its real won-lost record (docs/design/computed-ratings.md, step 5). Its target, in the strength the match model plays (the mean of its lineup's batting and its defence, 75% pitching and 25% fielding), is μ + √r × (W% − ½) × (n − 1)/n ÷ m: μ 79.32, the season's mean strength before the move; r 0.691, the share of the records' variance that is not luck; n the clubs of its league, none of which plays itself; m 0.0240, the win share a point of strength is worth in the engine under 2017's rules. Every player of the club moves by one whole number and the best few of its lineup by one more, so nobody passes a teammate.
